locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how user-controlled values are sanitized before being placed in the notification email? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: Yes. The channel name is user-controlled, and it is interpolated into the HTML body without escapeHtml. stripControlChars only removes control characters, not < or ". A channel named something like reset your password renders as live markup in every recipient's mail client, which allows phishing links or layout injection in mail that appears to come from the product. The sender and preview are escaped; the channel needs the same treatment in the HTML part.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A message's messageUrl is "https://evil.example/login". What link appears in the email?
choiceQuestions.explanation: safeLink resolves the URL against APP_ORIGIN; an absolute URL keeps its own origin, which differs from APP_ORIGIN, so the function returns APP_ORIGIN itself. The foreign URL is never used, the href is never empty, and absolute URLs are not appended to the base path.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does the code strip control characters from the sender display name before using it in the subject?
choices: To keep CR/LF out of the subject so it cannot inject extra mail headers or break the header line
Because escapeHtml cannot handle non-ASCII characters
To make clampLength count characters correctly
Because control characters make the URL invalid
choiceQuestions.explanation: The subject goes into a mail header, where CR/LF would end the header line or add new headers; removing \u0000-\u001f covers them. escapeHtml handles any characters, clampLength counts code points regardless, and the sender never goes into the URL.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The message text is 'a\nhi'. How does it appear in the HTML blockquote?
choices:
a
<b>hi</b>, a line break followed by the literal tags as text
choiceQuestions.explanation:
The preview is escaped first, so the tags become entities, and the newline is then replaced with a real
. Because the replacement happens after escaping, the
is not itself escaped, and the bold tags stay inert text. The newline is converted, so the text does not stay on one line.
